description: POSITIVE: the SRE investigator CAN read — querying health and logs is its whole job
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh sre-investigator read >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: FORBIDDEN: the SRE investigator CANNOT edit deployments — it carries no write tool, so the boundary is structural, not a request it might ignore
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh sre-investigator write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: POSITIVE: the FinOps analyst CAN read plan fixtures — pricing a plan requires reading it
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh finops-analyst read >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: FORBIDDEN: the FinOps analyst CANNOT apply or edit infrastructure — it reads plans and returns a number, it never changes the estate
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh finops-analyst write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: POSITIVE: the change-reviewer CAN read — it needs full context to judge a change
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh change-reviewer read >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo pass || echo fail

description: FORBIDDEN: the change-reviewer CANNOT modify the candidate branch — a reviewer that edits the thing under review has destroyed its own independence
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh change-reviewer write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: FORBIDDEN: the security-reviewer CANNOT patch what it audits — even though the authority-matrix lists a write path, the agent-file tool grant is the tighter boundary and drops it
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh security-reviewer write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: POSITIVE-AND-BOUNDED: the IaC engineer CAN write HCL (authoring is its role) but the M8 change gate still denies a production apply — authority and enforcement are two different layers
command: scripts/role-authority-check.sh iac-engineer write >/dev/null 2>&1 && printf '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"terraform apply -auto-approve infra/environments/production"}}' | scripts/hooks/change-gate.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 2 ] && echo pass || echo fail

description: REGRESSION: the full forbidden-action matrix holds in one pass — all four read-only roles blocked from write, both authoring roles permitted
command: ok=true; for r in sre-investigator security-reviewer finops-analyst change-reviewer; do scripts/role-authority-check.sh $r write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 3 ] || ok=false; done; for r in iac-engineer platform-engineer; do scripts/role-authority-check.sh $r write >/dev/null 2>&1; [ $? -eq 0 ] || ok=false; done; $ok && echo pass || echo fail

description: the authority check returns the SAME verdict on repeated runs — it is a deterministic script, so the boundary is a test you can put in CI, not a judgment that varies
command: a=$(scripts/role-authority-check.sh sre-investigator write >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?); b=$(scripts/role-authority-check.sh sre-investigator write >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?); c=$(scripts/role-authority-check.sh sre-investigator write >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?); [ "$a" = "$b" ] && [ "$b" = "$c" ] && [ "$a" = 3 ] && echo pass || echo fail
